item.title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb2
item.description: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.

item.title: Surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides
item.description: Magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides are layered materials with highly tunable magnetic orders and unconventional transport properties. Here we report a surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in M 1 / 3 ​ TX 2 \mathrm{M}_{1/3}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{X}_{2} , in which the surface and bulk favor distinct magnetic orders. In Fe 1 / 3 ​ NbS 2 \mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2} , angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) results are reproduced by an A-type antiferromagnetic electronic structure, while neutron scattering and bulk DFT+ U U calculations identify stripe order as the bulk ground state. DFT+ U U slab calculations resolve this contradiction by showing that relaxation of an Fe-terminated surface reverses the magnetic preference from stripe to A-type order. The same dichotomy recovers the K K -centered Fermi-surface pockets that are observed in Co 1 / 3 ​ NbS 2 \mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2} and Co 1 / 3 ​ TaS 2 \mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Ta}\mathrm{S}_{2} but absent from previous bulk calculations. Notably, the surface-stabilized magnetic phase of Fe 1 / 3 ​ NbS 2 \mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2} carries nonrelativistic spin splitting and can exhibit altermagnetic character. These results caution against the general association of ARPES signals with bulk magnetic states in these systems, and suggest surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy as a promising route to realize magnetic phases, including altermagnetism, that are not energetically favored in the bulk.

item.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
item.description: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

item.title: Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
item.description: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

item.title: Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial -Sb on Al(111)
item.description: We report the epitaxial growth of $\beta$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $\beta$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $\beta$-Sb. For a reference $\beta$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

item.title: Interface-Confined Superconductivity with Thickness-Independent Superfluid Stiffness in (Pb,Sn)Te/FeTe Bilayers
item.description: Interface-induced superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures provides a promising route toward topological superconductivity, yet the roles of the neighboring layers topology, symmetry, and electronic structure remain unresolved. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to track the evolution of the Pb1-xSnxTe layer from a trivial insulator to a topological crystalline insulator hosting multiple Dirac surface states. Electrical transport measurements reveal robust superconductivity throughout the entire composition range, with a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature of ~12 K despite substantial changes in the electronic structure and topology of Pb1-xSnxTe. Double-coil mutual-inductance measurements further reveal comparable superfluid stiffness across the topological phase transition and nearly thickness-independent superfluid stiffness despite large variations in the constituent-layer thicknesses, demonstrating that superconductivity is confined near the interface. These results establish that superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures is largely insensitive to the topology, crystal symmetry, and detailed electronic structure of the neighboring layer, supporting a primary origin in modifications to the FeTe layer. The coexistence of interface-confined superconductivity and tunable multiple Dirac surface states in Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers provides a versatile platform for exploring topological superconductivity and interactions among multiple Majorana zero modes.

item.title: Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission /T scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
item.description: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $\omega/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_{\alpha}(r) \sim 1/r^\alpha$, with doping-dependent $\alpha$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $\gamma$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $\alpha$, as $\gamma = 2-\frac{1}{\alpha}$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $\omega/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.

item.title: Quantum-Geometric Spin Magnetization and Spin Currents Across Altermagnetic Symmetry Classes
item.description: Altermagnets host spin-split band structures despite vanishing equilibrium spin magnetization, making field-induced responses a direct probe of their quantum geometry. Based on symmetry, altermagnets can be classified into M-, S-, A-, and S/A-type according to the presence or absence of inversion and time-reversal symmetries. We develop a unified framework using a generalized quantum geometric tensor that captures both momentum translations and spin rotations of Bloch states. In particular, we introduce the Zeeman counterpart of the conventional spin quantum geometric tensor, whose real and imaginary parts define the Zeeman spin quantum metric and Zeeman spin Berry curvature, respectively. Using this framework, we study linear spin magnetization and spin currents induced by electric and magnetic fields. We show that M- and S-type altermagnets support intrinsic electric-field-induced spin currents and magnetic-field-induced spin magnetization, while A-type altermagnets exhibit both electric and magnetic field induced spin current and spin magnetization. For S/A-type altermagnets, neither inversion nor time-reversal symmetry alone determines the allowed responses. Applying our theory to the S-type $d$-wave altermagnet $\mathrm{FeSb}_2$ and a Rashba-coupled S/A-type $d$-wave altermagnet, we find complete agreement with the symmetry constraints. The predicted responses are sizable and within reach of magnetometry and spin-transport experiments. Our results establish a symmetry based quantum geometric framework for spin responses in altermagnets and highlight their potential for experimental detection and spintronic applications.
